sections.overview: The grey heron is a widespread wading bird that hunts by waiting or moving slowly through shallow water.
sections.identification: It has a grey back, pale neck, dark head stripe and long bill; in flight it folds its neck into an S shape.
sections.habitat: It forages around lakes, rivers, marshes and estuaries, including both fresh and brackish waters.
sections.diet: Fish are frequent prey, but it also takes amphibians, small mammals and other animals within striking range.
sections.behavior: A heron may remain motionless before striking rapidly with its bill; individuals often feed alone.
sections.reproduction: It commonly nests colonially in trees, in groups known as heronries.
sections.ecology: Its varied prey links wetland food webs, and its feeding range can extend beyond the water’s edge.
sections.conservation: The RSPB lists the species as Green in its UK conservation-status system; this is a regional assessment.
